passage:
Keerthana: Deepa got the team lead role. announced 10 mins ago
Sahil: oh. you wanted that
Keerthana: I'm so annoyed I can't even look at my screen 😠
Sahil: fair. want to rant?
Keerthana: I did rant. to my notebook. then I made myself write 3 lists
Sahil: of?
Keerthana: what I have: a job I'm good at, a team that trusts me, the Pune transfer I asked for
Keerthana: what I control: the certification in March, and asking my manager what the gap was
Keerthana: and me 2 years ago: an intern making tea for everyone
Sahil: that's a pretty good list tbh
Keerthana: I still want to lead a team. just not while stewing about Deepa
Sahil: proud of you 🙂 coffee after work?
Keerthana: yes. and I'll congratulate her properly first

qa.q: What was Keerthana two years ago?
qa.a: An intern making tea for everyone.

qa.q: How did Keerthana feel when Deepa's promotion was announced?
qa.a: Keerthana was so annoyed that even looking at the screen felt impossible.

qa.q: What did Keerthana choose to do with the anger, and why did it help?
qa.a: Keerthana wrote three lists, of what Keerthana has, what Keerthana controls and where Keerthana was two years ago, which kept the ambition while letting the envy cool.

qa.q: How might Deepa feel when Keerthana congratulates her properly?
qa.a: Deepa may feel supported and relieved, since a colleague who wanted the role is choosing warmth over resentment.

grounding: A young professional fuming at a peer's promotion lists what they have, what they control and how far they have come, keeping ambition without letting envy rule.

passage: The news reached the kasba branch of the cooperative bank before lunch: Ramesh, who had joined on the same day as Jatin, was now assistant branch officer. Jatin smiled and shook his hand, then sat at his counter with his jaw clenched. Ramesh would now sign his leave forms. On the bus home, past the sugarcane fields, Jatin caught the thought going round and round: why him, why not me? He made himself stop. What did he actually have? A steady job four kilometres from his parents, a wife who laughed at his jokes, a scooter fully paid off. What could he control? The officer exam in June, and asking the manager what Ramesh had done that he hadn't. Three years ago he had been jobless, filling in forms at the cyber cafe. By the time he got home, he still wanted the post. He just wasn't angry about it.

qa.q: What post did Ramesh get?
qa.a: Assistant branch officer.

qa.q: What was Jatin feeling at his counter after shaking Ramesh's hand?
qa.a: Under the smile he felt envious and resentful, his jaw clenched at the thought of Ramesh signing his leave forms.

qa.q: What questions did Jatin ask himself on the bus, and how did they help?
qa.a: What he actually has and what he can control, plus remembering being jobless three years ago, which let him keep wanting the post without the anger.

qa.q: How might Ramesh feel if Jatin had stayed resentful?
qa.a: Ramesh might sense coldness from someone he joined with, making the new role lonelier.

grounding: A young bank clerk fuming at a peer's promotion asks what he has and can control and compares with his own past, keeping ambition without envy.

passage: When the email went round the Toronto design studio announcing that Rania was now senior designer, Kwame felt his face go hot. They'd started the same month. He had stayed later, he told himself. He walked out for coffee to stop himself typing anything. In the queue he did what his older sister always told him: ask three questions. What do I have? A job I like, a portfolio twice as strong as last year's, a mentor who answers my messages. What can I control? My next project, and asking my lead exactly what senior means here. Where was I two years ago? Driving deliveries and sketching on my breaks. By the time his coffee came, the heat had gone. He went back in, stopped at Rania's desk and said, "Congratulations. Can you show me how you pitched the museum brief?"

qa.q: What was Kwame doing two years ago?
qa.a: Driving deliveries and sketching on his breaks.

qa.q: What was Kwame feeling when he read the email about Rania?
qa.a: His face went hot; he felt envious and hard done by, telling himself he had stayed later.

qa.q: Which of Kwame's choices shows he kept his ambition without the envy?
qa.a: Going back to congratulate Rania and asking how Rania pitched the museum brief, turning envy into a chance to learn.

qa.q: How might Rania see Kwame's question at Rania's desk?
qa.a: Rania may feel respected and glad that a peer who started the same month is congratulating and learning rather than resenting.

passage: The staff room went quiet when the principal pinned up the notice: Hrithik Sir, head of the science department. Tejas, twenty-five, who had joined the school the same year, kept marking Class 8 notebooks. His red pen pressed so hard it tore a page. Hrithik came in, and Tejas said, "Congratulations," in a voice he barely recognised. At break he stood by the water cooler and made himself ask, silently: what do I actually have? A job he loved, children who stayed back to ask questions, the science club he started. What can I control? Finishing his B.Ed. project, and asking the principal what the post needed. Three years ago he had been tutoring in a rented room. He still wanted to lead a department one day. He went back and asked Hrithik if the science club could use the lab on Fridays.

qa.q: What post did Hrithik get?
qa.a: He became head of the science department.

qa.q: What does Tejas's red pen tearing a page suggest?
qa.a: It suggests he is fuming with envy and frustration, even while keeping quiet in the staff room.

qa.q: Which choice by Tejas helped him most, and why?
qa.a: Asking himself what he has, what he can control and where he was three years ago let him keep his ambition without letting envy take over his day.

qa.q: How might Hrithik see Tejas when he asks about the lab on Fridays?
qa.a: Hrithik might be relieved that Tejas is working with him rather than against him, and more willing to support the science club.

grounding: A young teacher catches himself fuming at a peer's promotion, counts what he has and can control, compares to his own past and keeps his ambition.

passage:
Dear Baljeet Paaji,

You asked in your last letter how the new job is going. Honestly, last Monday I almost wrote to you in a rage. Arun, who joined the kitchen a month after me, was made sous chef. I spent the whole dinner service slamming pans.

Then I remembered what you told me when I was washing dishes at your dhaba: "Count what's in your hands before you count what's in someone else's." So I did. I have a job in a proper hotel kitchen. The head chef trusts me with the tandoor. I've learned three new sauces this year. What can I control? My knife speed, which is still slow, and asking chef what Arun did that I didn't. And four years ago I couldn't make a round roti.

I still want that sous chef coat. I'm just not angry about it any more.

With respect,
Lokesh

qa.q: Who was made sous chef?
qa.a: Arun, who joined the kitchen a month after Lokesh, was made sous chef.

qa.q: How did Lokesh feel on the Monday Arun was promoted?
qa.a: Lokesh was furious and envious, so angry that the whole dinner service went in slamming pans.

qa.q: What helped Lokesh turn that anger into something useful?
qa.a: Remembering Baljeet's advice, Lokesh counted what was in hand, named what could be controlled and looked back four years, keeping the goal without the anger.

qa.q: How might Baljeet feel reading this letter?
qa.a: Baljeet would likely feel proud that Lokesh remembered the advice from the dhaba days and used it to handle a hard moment.

grounding: A young cook fuming at a peer's promotion looks at what is in hand, what can be controlled and how far the journey has come, and keeps ambition without envy.
